coverage: Covering roughly Nov 17–18, 2026. Compiled Wednesday, ET.
note: Anthropic's IPO is expected Thursday, per posts in your feed.

items.headline: Nvidia's board says it will not bring Jensen Huang back, on a blowout earnings night
items.summary: On the earnings call, interim CEO Colette Kress said Huang resigned, the board accepted it and "will not reinstate Jensen," per @firesidealpha. Hours later Semafor reported a board faction is still pushing for his return, and that Huang has spoken with at least one director about it, @KobeissiLetter noted. Shopify's Tobi Lütke, quoted by @davidsenra, argued there is no succession for a founder like him.
items.short: The board says no to Huang's return; a faction reportedly disagrees.

items.headline: Nvidia's numbers: "demand far exceeds supply"
items.summary: Revenue grew 103% from a year ago and EPS 106%, with a $380B buyback, @MrMikeInvesting summarized. @aleabitoreddit pulled the industry read-through: supply commitments jumped from $279B to $390B, mostly multi-year memory procurement; Nvidia guided to about 75% growth; it put the industry cloud backlog at $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion, with Hopper rentals at 2x original pricing; and co-packaged optics switches are in volume production.
items.short: Revenue +103%, memory commitments up to $390B, GPU rental prices rising.

items.headline: Nvidia says it will keep backing neoclouds, more selectively
items.summary: Nvidia called neoclouds "an increasingly important part of the global AI infrastructure ecosystem" but said it will be "disciplined in how we commit capital," @ren_stocks quoted. @daniel_koss read it as Nvidia starting to pick winners, with Nebius and CoreWeave the obvious ones; @babyfolio noted the call did not announce a blanket stop to neocloud financing.
items.short: Support continues, with more discipline on who gets capital.

items.author: Rose Celine Investments 🌹
items.text:
The Stock Price Is Not the Business

If you weren’t so excited when your stocks went up, you probably wouldn’t be so disappointed when they went down.

When you own a business, just like when you’re in a marriage or any long term relationship, there will be good times and bad times. There will be tailwinds and headwinds. Some years everything seems to go your way, and other years nothing does. That doesn’t necessarily mean the relationship is broken or the business has become less valuable. …

items.author: Paul Millerd
items.text:
Ive probably talked to over 1000 people who are contemplating leaving their job or making a change. 

There’s basically two camps
1. They must leave.  They just want friends, advice, or ideas to make it smoother.  

2. The stuck but afraid: don’t like what they’re doing now but have incredibly detailed pictures and stories about what could go wrong

Almost everyone in camp one makes some sort of leap. They rarely “go back”

the majority of camp two don’t make a major change and if they do probably half of those return to their previous positions

The difference between $COHR & $AAOI gets clearer every day. 

One is an elite company with a clean balance sheet. The other one is constantly diluting shareholders.

quoted.author: KaizenInvestor
quoted.text:
I think both $AAOI and $COHR can benefit from the $LITE x $MRVL takeover. 

$AVGO will look at alternative suppliers and both companies can fill that gap. 

I decided to buy Coherent yesterday because I think they have a significantly better risk/reward at the moment. 

The first difference is that Coherent already has a proven and trustworthy management team. The management of AAOI on the other hand, has proven during earnings yesterday that you can’t always trust their estimates and predictions. 

Another point I find important is that Coherent is already profitable. AAOI still burns cash every on a yearly basis and relies heavily on ATMs. 

The technology of Coherent is also proven and they have a multi-year strategic agreement with Nvidia. The collaboration focuses on advancing the optics technologies. 

The last thing is valuation, the only thing we can compare here is the P/S, as AAOI is not profitable yet. The P/S of Coherent is half of that of AAOI at the moment. 

So, it is not because AAOI has a smaller market cap that they are cheaper. I think Coherent is a cheaper buy and a more proven and a high quality buy at the moment.

items.title: Takeaways from Jensen Huang on the BG2 podcast
items.author: Boring_Business
items.summary: Fifteen notes from Huang's 90-minute talk with Brad Gerstner, worth rereading the week he left. Inference and reasoning drive compute demand; cheaper intelligence leads to far more use; Moore's law is over, so waiting a year now costs more, not less; and he sees global compute spend heading from about $1T toward $10T a year.

items.title: Why a conservative investor went 60% AI
items.author: The Fundamentalist
items.summary: A once-cautious investor explains a concentrated bet on AI by sorting people into heavy, basic and non-users of AI, and arguing that the skeptics mostly come from the last two groups. It quotes a long post on the widening gap between what the public sees and what frontier users see. Read it as a statement of the bull case, and of what concentration feels like from the inside.

items.title: Four Cards
items.rule: If a parcel is marked Express, it has a red sticker.
items.explanation: Express could hide something that breaks the rule; Blue sticker breaks it if the other side turns out to be Express. Red sticker can't break it (the rule never says only those cards have it), and Standard isn't covered by the rule at all. Most people pick the card that matches the rule's second half instead of the one that could falsify it.

items.author: Milk Road AI
items.text:
According to Korean media, the KOSPI opened UP 2.6% this morning at 5,098 after Nvidia's earnings.

Samsung jumped about 4% at the open and SK Hynix jumped almost 6%.

Then retail investors started selling, and by late morning the KOSPI was back below 5,000.

The market recovered in the afternoon. The KOSPI closed at 5,067, up about 2%. Samsung finished up about 2.3% and SK Hynix finished up about 4.2%.

We think this tells you a lot about where sentiment is. Nvidia just posted a record quarter and said demand far exceeds supply, and people still sold the rip for most of the morning. …
